summary: Task 5 (background review listener, first-ever inbound Telegram path) is sound. Every state-changing action funnels through resolve_dedup_callback's fail-closed numeric-admin gate, which runs before any token/queue lookup; the callback_data parser rejects anything outside the exact dd:<c|k>:<token> grammar (non-str, oversized, malformed, wrong prefix, unicode lookalikes) without I/O; the token is only ever used as a bound SQLite parameter, so no injection surface exists; allowed_updates=['callback_query'] is set; getUpdates is a real 30s long-poll so no busy-loop; 409 Conflict gets a distinct 60s backoff with an operator-facing single-listener message, generic errors get 5s backoff, and both are exercised by tests; offset is advanced before the per-update handler runs so a poisoned update can't be redelivered forever, and each update's exception is caught individually so the loop/thread survives; edited-message content is the (already-redacted) original alert text plus one of a small fixed set of status strings — no token or secret ever appears in chat or in the operator-decision INFO log (action + link + status only). Full existing suite (1324 tests) plus the 10 new ReviewListener tests pass with no regressions.

findings.description: _handle_review_update calls pending_repo.get_review_token_link(token) unconditionally for every syntactically-valid dd:<c|k>:<token> callback, BEFORE resolve_dedup_callback's admin check runs. resolve_dedup_callback's own docstring states the admin gate is meant to run 'FIRST, before any token lookup' precisely so a non-admin press costs nothing; the Task-5 handler's pre-fetch (needed only to have the link available for the INFO log line, since resolve_dedup_callback deletes the token on terminal outcomes) reintroduces one SQLite open+query ahead of that gate for every well-formed callback, including from a non-admin.
findings.impact: Not exploitable as a meaningful DoS today: a callback_query can only be generated by pressing a real inline button on a message the presser can see, and the only messages carrying dd: buttons are private 1:1 alerts to TELEGRAM_ADMIN_ID, so the reachable population of 'non-admin' pressers is effectively empty under the current architecture. This is a hardening/defense-in-depth gap, not a live vulnerability: if this listener or its buttons are ever exposed to a wider chat (group/channel) the extra read-before-auth would become a real per-message DB-read amplification vector for strangers.
findings.recommendation: Check from_user.id against the admin id (or call a cheap prefix of resolve_dedup_callback's own gate) before the get_review_token_link pre-fetch, and only fetch the link for logging on the admin path. Low priority; does not block merge.

findings.location: news_bot.py: _run_review_listener per-update except block ('logger.exception("[review] failed to handle update %s — skipped", ...)')
findings.description: _TokenRedactingFilter (installed on the root logger/handlers) scrubs record.msg/record.args, but NOT the exc_info-rendered traceback text that logger.exception() appends via the handler's Formatter — so if an underlying exception's own str() ever embedded the raw TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN (e.g. a bot-API URL), that traceback line would bypass the redaction filter. This is the same pattern already used elsewhere in news_bot.py (logger.exception at L887/894/2320/2461/2862/2887), not something Task 5 introduces uniquely.
findings.impact: Verified empirically (local httpx repro) that the transport errors actually reachable through python-telegram-bot 21.10's HTTPXRequest.do_request (httpx.ConnectError/TimeoutException wrapped into telegram.error.NetworkError/TimedOut) do not embed the request URL or token in their str() today, and the listener's own poll-failure/Conflict except-blocks already run exceptions through sanitize_error_message() before logging. So this is a latent, largely theoretical gap consistent with an existing accepted codebase pattern rather than a new, practically exploitable leak.
findings.recommendation: Optional hardening, not blocking: route the per-update catch-all through sanitize_error_message(exc) in the log message (as the poll-level except blocks already do) for defense-in-depth, or accept as a pre-existing, low-risk pattern shared across the codebase.

checks_performed: Grammar parser (_parse_review_callback_data): non-str, None, empty, garbage, wrong prefix, unknown letter, full-word action on the wire, missing/extra fields, empty token, oversized payload, unicode-homoglyph colon — all safely rejected before any I/O; token only ever used as a bound sqlite3 parameter (no injection).

Auth path: confirmed every pending_repo write (skip_pending/delete_review_token/put_review_token) lives inside resolve_dedup_callback, whose numeric-admin check is the first statement and fails closed on non-numeric TELEGRAM_ADMIN_ID or from_user_id; Task-5 handler performs no direct state-changing call (only one read, see SEC-T5-1).

DoS: allowed_updates=['callback_query'] set; get_updates is a genuine 30s long-poll (no busy loop); per-batch size bounded by Telegram's own default; 5s generic backoff / 60s Conflict backoff verified by tests with patched-to-0 constants + stop_event seam; offset advanced before per-update dispatch so a poisoned update is acked exactly once; per-update and per-poll exceptions independently caught so neither one bad update nor a network blip can kill the thread or spin the CPU.

Info leak: edited message = _redact_text'd original alert text + one of resolve_dedup_callback's fixed status strings (never the token); operator-decision INFO log = action + link (public article URL) + status only, no token; startup/warning pings contain no secret values.
409 handling: dedicated Conflict except-branch, 60s backoff, explicit single-listener operator message; exercised by test_review_listener_conflict_409_logged_with_backoff.
Full regression: pytest tests/test_integration.py -k ReviewListener -q → 10 passed; full suite pytest -q → 1324 passed, no regressions.
